title: Blog: Launch post for Latency/$ benchmark report (charts, CTAs, disclosures, SEO)
author: Elliot Price
body:
## Summary
This PR adds the public launch blog post for Redwood’s Latency/$ benchmark report.

The post is intended to (1) explain “production economics” in practical engineering terms, (2) summarize the major findings with embedded charts, (3) drive readers to the report PDF + landing page, and (4) set expectations with explicit methodology/disclosure language (variance, region differences, workload scope, and what is/isn’t being claimed).

## What’s included
- New blog post markdown with:
  - SEO frontmatter (title/description/canonical, OpenGraph, twitter card)
  - Above-the-fold CTA + mid-article + end CTA variants (download report / try hosted API / talk to an expert)
  - Embedded charts (exported PNG + lightweight caption/alt text)
  - “How to interpret results” + methodology disclosure section aligned to public-claims guidelines
  - FAQ accordion section (variance, caching/batching, cost assumptions, region selection)
- Link hygiene:
  - All internal links are relative and verified in preview
  - External links pinned to stable URLs where possible
  - Added the report landing page + methodology appendix links
- Broken-link checks + basic SEO validation notes in PR

## Screenshots / Preview
- Local preview: `pnpm dev` → /blog/latency-per-dollar-benchmark-launch
- Chart rendering verified in light/dark mode
- Mobile layout: CTA buttons stack correctly; chart captions don’t overflow

## Disclosure / claims guardrails (important)
The post intentionally avoids absolute/blanket claims (e.g., “fastest”, “best”) and instead:
- Uses “in our measurements” language
- States workloads covered (chat + embeddings baseline) and that results depend on request mix/concurrency/sequence lengths
- Notes variance and confidence language (repeat runs, rerun policy, no cherry-picking)
- Clarifies that published tables are a sanitized subset (no per-request logs, no customer-identifying telemetry)

## QA
- ✅ `pnpm lint`
- ✅ `pnpm test`
- ✅ `pnpm build`
- ✅ `pnpm check:links` (no broken internal links)
- ✅ Lighthouse snapshot (preview): no regressions vs baseline for blog template

## Files changed (high level)
- `content/blog/2025-02-26-latency-per-dollar-benchmark-launch.md` (new)
- `public/assets/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar/*.png` (new chart exports)
- `components/BlogCta/BenchmarkReportCta.tsx` (new CTA block; used by this post)
- `components/Disclosure/BenchmarkDisclosure.tsx` (new disclosure callout shared across benchmark pages)
- `lib/seo/canonical.ts` (small helper to prevent accidental duplicate canonicals)
- `scripts/check-links.ts` (include blog content dir + allowlist for known redirects)

## Notable snippets
### Frontmatter (SEO)
- title: "Latency per dollar: a benchmark report on production economics for LLM inference"
- description: "A reproducible benchmark across popular open models and regions, reporting latency/$ with methodology disclosures and guidance on interpretation."
- canonical: "https://redwoodinference.com/blog/latency-per-dollar-benchmark-report"

### Disclosure block (excerpt)
"These results reflect Redwood-run benchmarks for the workloads and configurations described in the methodology appendix. Performance and cost will vary with request mix, concurrency, sequence lengths, routing policies, and regional capacity. We report variance across repeat runs and rerun anomalous results per our internal triage policy. We do not publish per-request logs or customer-identifying traces."

## Commits
1) `docs(blog): add benchmark launch post draft + structure`
2) `docs(charts): add exported chart assets + captions/alt text`
3) `docs(cta): add BenchmarkReportCta block + tracking params`
4) `docs(disclosure): add reusable benchmark disclosure component`
5) `chore(seo): canonical helper + fix meta description length`
6) `chore(linkcheck): expand link checker to blog content + allowlist`

---

# Review conversation (highlights)

**Renee Sullivan** (comment): “CTA in the first 2 paragraphs feels a bit salesy. Can we move it below the definition of latency/$ so it reads like an engineering post first?”

**Elliot Price** (reply): “Agreed. Updated hero to keep the first CTA as a low-friction ‘Download the report’ link, moved ‘Talk to an expert’ to mid-article after the ‘How to use these numbers’ section.”

**Soojin Lee** (comment): “Headline sentence ‘best latency per dollar across regions’ is too absolute. Please align with messaging doc: ‘leading’ / ‘in our measurements’ / avoid superlatives unless scoped.”

**Elliot Price** (reply): “Fixed language throughout. Added a short callout under the first chart: ‘in our measurements’ + link to methodology.”

**Claire Dubois** (comment): “Chart 2 caption should specify p50 vs p95. Also we should explicitly say the cost denominator is $/1M output tokens for the run config; otherwise people will assume blended invoice cost.”

**Elliot Price** (reply): “Updated captions and added a footnote in the disclosure block. Also added an FAQ item: ‘What does the $ represent?’”

**Jonas Weber** (comment): “Please add one sentence acknowledging caching/batching policy: readers will ask if we optimized only for benchmark.”

**Elliot Price** (reply): “Added line: ‘We use consistent caching/batching settings across regions per the methodology; we do not tune per-model settings for the published run set.’”

**Michael Grant** (comment): “The sentence ‘apples-to-apples across regions’ needs a qualifier. We should avoid implying identical market pricing or network paths. Suggest: ‘controlled to be comparable’.”

**Elliot Price** (reply): “Done. Replaced with ‘configured to be comparable’ and added qualifier about network path variability.”

**Wei Chen** (comment): “One internal link points to `/docs/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar` but the landing page PR uses `/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar`. Linkcheck currently passes because it’s treated as external. Please update.”

**Elliot Price** (reply): “Good catch. Fixed link + updated linkcheck to treat `redwoodinference.com` as internal for path validation in preview.”
